sentences.text: Judgment

The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 14.06.2024.
2.

The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 14.06.2024 at about 11.30 a.m., the petitioner was riding a Motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-03-JF-7764 proceeding on Yalachahalli village, Volvo Factory near Bangalore to Kolar NH-75 road, Nandagudi Hobli,
Bengaluru, at that time an Auto-Rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-08-5647 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life, without following any traffic rules, came at high speed against one way and dashed against the petitioner motorcycle.
Due to forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained several grievous injuries.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to MVJ Hospital, there after shifted to Victoria Hospital and again shifted to MVJ Hospital,
wherein he was admitted as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 29 years, the petitioner was working as Salesmand and earning Rs.24,000/- per month.

Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner Abdul Mateen vs Future India Gen Ins Co Ltd on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110525736/
2 has become permanently disabled and unable to look after the said work.

sentences.text: Respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Hence,
both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notice, both the respondents appeared through their counsels and filed their respective written statements.

The respondent No.1 in its written statement denied the allegations made in the plaint and submitted that, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.
KA-08-5647 and contended that petitioner himself was riding his motorcycle in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Auto-rickshaw.
Further, the driver of the Auto-rickshaw was not holding valid and effective driving license, which is in contravention of the policy conditions.
Further, the Auto-rickshaw was not having valid permit and fitness certificate as on date of accident and at the time of alleged accident the petitioner was not wearing safety head-gear.

The respondent No.2 in its written statement denied the allegations made in the plaint and submitted that, this respondent is the absolute owner of the Auto- rickshaw bearing Reg. No.
KA-08-5647 and is duly insured with the respondent No.1 and policy was inforce as on the date of accident and liability is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further both the respondents denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. On the basis of above pleadings, following issues are Re-framed:

1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he is the victim of the motor vehicle accident caused by the driver of the Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-08-5647 on 14.06.2024 at about 11.30 a.m., near Yalachahalli village, Volvo Factory near Bangalore to Kolar NH-75 Road, Nangagudi Hobli, Bengaluru Rural and sustained injuries as pleaded in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or Award?

13. It must be noted that, in the cross- examination of PW.1, it is suggested by the learned counsel for respondent No.1 that, the accident had happened because of the negligence on the part of rider of the motorcycle, but witness denied the said suggestion.
No matter whether PW.1 admits the said suggestion or not, but in my opinion, the said suggestion is sufficient to conclude that, respondents have admitted the accident.
14. The next question would be, on whose fault accident has occurred.

This question arises because at para No.8 of the written statement filed by respondent No.1, in which the respondent No.1 has raised the specific defence that, the accident had happened due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
Thus, the question would be whether this say of the respondent No.1 can be accepted or not.

It is true that, in the cross-examination of petitioner/PW.1, learned counsel for respondent No.1 has posed question to the PW.1 that, accident is happened due to the negligence of petitioner himself,
but PW.1 had denied the said suggestion.
However, it is important to note that, the second respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Further, the second respondent has not adduced any evidence before the Court.
Besides, the respondents have not examined the rider of the aforesaid motorcycle.
Thus, these facts, make it clear that, except allegations, the respondent No.1 has not made any efforts to show that, accident had happened because of the fault of the rider of motorcycle.
In addition to that, all the police documents clearly shows that, driver of the offending vehicle i.e., Auto-rickshaw drove his auto in one-way road against traffic flow.
Meaning thereby the act of the driver of offending vehicle is contraflow driving, which is against the traffic rules.

In view of above discussion this Tribunal opine that, due to the rash and negligent driving of the auto- rickshaw, that too in the wrong side in one-way, against direction of traffic rules, accident had happened.
15. The next question would be, whether the petitioner sustained injuries in the accident or not.
It must be noted that, the Ex.P.6 i.e., Wound Certificate shows that, the petitioner was admitted to MVJ Medical College and Research Hospital on 14.06.2024.

the injury sustained by the petitioner is grievous in nature.

These facts are not denied by the respondent No.1.

Hence, these facts are sufficient to conclude that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Auto- Rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-08-5647.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
16. ISSUE No.2:
The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to MVJ Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he took treatment as inpatient.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, he is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

Hence,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:

sentences.text: The petitioner has produced the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.11 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the MVJ Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient for totally 06 days.

He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.6, which reveals that, petitioner has sustained the following injuries:
(i) Left femur shaft fracture (closed)
(ii) Parieto-frontal sub-dual hemorrhage.
and the doctor has opined that the injuries are grievous in nature.
Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
18. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
However in support of his plea, he has produced medical bills which is marked at Ex.P.12 to the tune of Rs.78,421/-.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.78,421/- towards medical expenses.
19. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.11 Discharge summary issued by MVJ Medical college and Research Hospital, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital for about 06 days.
Hence, at least 01 month is required to recover from the accidental injuries.
It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was working as Salesman and earning Rs.24,000/- per month, in support of his income he has not produced any single document.

So, in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.16,500/- as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2024 at Rs.16,500/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench.

sentences.text: The accident is of the year is 2024.
Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- p.m. as per above decision.
Hence, 01 month is to be considered as loss of income.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,500/- under this head.
20. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability-
The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. Nagaraj B. N in order to substantiate the same, PW.3 has produced documents marked at Ex.P.18 and Ex.P.19.

Admittedly,
the PW.3 is not a treated doctor.
He was sworn that, petitioner has got Disability of 16% to the whole body, but he has not issued the disability certificate.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor and evidence given by the petitioner himself before the Court, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 11%,
cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, this Tribunal consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 11%.

Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner/injured has to be determined.
Ex.P.13 is the Aadhar Card of the petitioner, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 05.11.2002 and accident took place in the year 2024.
Accordingly, I assess his age as 22 years at the time of this accident.
As per the ruling reported in AIR 2009 SCW page-3014 between SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS, the relevant multiplier applicable is '18'.

21. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES:
Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in MVJ Hospital, Bangalore as inpatient from 15.06.2024 to 21.06.2024 i.e., for 06 days.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges.
22. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The petitioner was aged about 22 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries.
However he might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life.
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and fracture, Rs.30,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness.
23. TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The petitioner has claimed towards future medical expenses.
The doctor who has been examined as PW.3 has suggested to undergo another surgery for the removal of the implants and the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
By keeping nature of the injuries sustained, as he is bound to suffer medical problems in future and cannot every time depend upon Government hospital.
Hence, under this head Rs.20,000/- is awarded.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,16,961/- under various heads.
24. LIABILITY:
In view of above discussion in Issue No.1, this Tribunal opine that, accident had happened due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-08- 5647.
Now the question before this Tribunal is that, whether insurance company is liable to indemnify the owner of the offending vehicle or not.

The learned counsel for petitioner argued that, accident had happened due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of the offending vehicle and as on the date of accident the said offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.2.
As such, he argued that, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The learned counsel for insurance company argued that, as on the date of accident owner of the offending vehicle did not have valid permit to fly the offending vehicle.
In support of his argument he relied upon the evidence of RW.1 as well as Ex.R.2 and Judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Civil Appeal No. 9322/2022 between Gohar Mohammed Vs. UPSRTC and others.

entities.text: Gohar Mohammed Vs. UPSRTC and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Tribunal perused the evidence of RW.1 as well as Ex.R.2, it goes to show that, as on the date of accident the owner of the offending vehicle did not have valid permit to fly his auto-rickshaw.

Further, on perusal of Judgment relied by the Insurance Company, wherein also offending vehicle was not plied as per the terms and conditions of the permit and also in violation of the terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy.
Considering the said fact, Hon'ble Apex Court upheld the findings of Hon'ble High Court of Allahabad and M.A.C.T that, owner of the offending vehicle was held liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, in view of above facts and circumstances as well as above discussions, respondent No.2 i.e., owner of the offending vehicle is held liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
25. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
